items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
items.full_text_snippet: TL;DR NVIDIA Kumo Relational is a pre-trained relational foundation model that makes predictions directly on enterprise databases. Given a predictive query, it gathers up to 10,000 historical examples as context and predicts outcomes such as churn, demand, or fraud in a single forward pass. It needs no task-specific training, no feature engineering, and no flattening of tables. Kumo Relational is the first few-shot foundation model to outperform supervised machine learning on common relational benchmarks. Across 41 tasks on 15 databases, it beats supervised relational deep learning models and expert-engineered gradient-boosted tree pipelines, and on the SAP SALT enterprise benchmark it surpasses AutoGluon ensembles by 8% in mean reciprocal rank (MRR). It scales to databases with 500B+ rows and works for humans and agents alike, through NVIDIA's open-source, GPU-native structured-data-models library or as an NVIDIA NIM. The Shift to Structured Data Foundation Models Foundation models have already rewritten the playbook for language and vision. Not long ago, production NLP meant a dedicated model per task, each fed by its own pipeline of tokenization, lemmatization, and n-grams. LLMs made that stack largely obsolete for three reasons: they were more accurate than the best task-specific models, far simpler to put into production, and flexible enough to open a new era of agentic applications. The same shift is now underway for structured data. Relational databases power the world's most critical business decisions, yet predictive modeling on them still requires weeks of feature engineering, task-specific training, and tuned pipelines. Structured data foundation models change that for the same three reasons: Better accuracy today: As drop-in replacements, these models already beat many production pipelines, especially XGBoost. They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. items.full_text_snippet: Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal . The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which include deals still in negotiation. And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers. Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during that same time period, with only two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales, according to the WSJ report. Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage. Last week, the company told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue alone has now reached $16.8 billion , up 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO. Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

items.full_text_snippet: We introduced EmbeddingGemma last year to provide a lightweight option for high-quality text embeddings, to help your apps organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware. The developer community’s response blew past our expectations. With more than 20 million downloads, builders have used it to power smarter on-device search tools and privacy-first retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. Today, we’re launching EmbeddingGemma 2 , expanding beyond text to unify code, images, video, and audio in a shared embedding space. Built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license, EmbeddingGemma 2 has 740 million parameters, making it optimal for on-device inference. It can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.

items.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
items.full_text_snippet: Models specialized for a domain or a task by fine-tuning general open-source models, such as Qwen and Gemma, inherit a vocabulary built for many domains and general applications. In an essay grader we run in production, that vocabulary split the text the model writes most into many tokens. This article previews some results from the VocabX paper, which we will publish soon: how we specialized the vocabulary around the cost of each token rather than its frequency, and cut measured inference cost by 77% without changing the base model. The tokenizer is usually treated as a fixed property of the base model, inherited and left alone. For a model specialized in a single domain, it can be one of the largest cost levers, and it is set before any training step. One of the systems we run in production is an automated grader for Portuguese essays, built on Qwen3-4B. It receives the essay, the prompt and the supporting texts, and returns a JSON assessment with a grade and a comment for each competency. The model was already small, at 4 billion parameters, and had already been trained for the task. Its tokenizer, however, was still the original Qwen3-4B one, built for many languages and many kinds of text. In the grader, it was used for a single language, Portuguese, and a single response format. That had two costs: the text the grader writes on every request took more tokens than it needed, and at every generated token the model scored a vocabulary of 151,669 entries, including many this task almost never uses. We rebuilt that vocabulary with a method we call VocabX, keeping the same base model, the same data and the same training recipe. The numbers in this article come from the current version of the paper, still under review, and may change before publication. items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 20 Oct 2026] Title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems View a PDF of the paper titled MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems, by Mohammad Kachuee and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> RSI三块关键拼图，MemT 1.0从模型层补上「记忆」 鹭羽 2026-10-20 20:50:34 来源： 量子位 鹭羽 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI AI圈，最近集体盯上了三个字母： RSI 。 Hinton的RSI论文 ，22位署名作者里，坐着Bengio、OpenAI首席科学家Pachocki、Anthropic联创Jack Clark……几乎AI的半壁江山都在这儿。 大家在将目光投向AI自我改进的同时，一个更值得追问的基础问题浮出水面： 一次改进，如何成为下一次的起点？ 有效的方法需要被保留，走过的弯路也需要被识别，承接这件事的，其实是 记忆 。 常规的思路很简单：给AI直接外接一个经验库，操作方法、历史教训就能通通被保存检索。 记忆张量 在这方面的探索，则给出了一份截然不同的答卷——记忆原生。 何为记忆原生？就是将经验的保留、更新和调用，做成模型可以学习的能力。 当记忆在模型中生根发芽，便构成了 记忆原生模型 。 其最新开源发布的 MemT 1.0 系列，就给出了一条颇为具体的路径： 它把经验编码成内部动态状态，再通过训练学习怎样写入、更新和读取，最后让这些状态经由记忆分支参与后续计算。 与外部记忆相比，它不仅能力没打折，未来拓展的天花板也会更高。 这也是记忆原生模型 首次 实现近300B参数规模的工程验证。 （论文地址指路： https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26825） 好家伙，记忆看不见摸不着，但却实打实成为模型成长的立足根本。 从早期要求模型记住信息，到用好经验，模型对记忆的要求不断升级，也让记忆一步步从幕后走到台前。 把记忆放进模型 MemT 1.0这次直接甩出两个型号： MemT-1.0-Nano 总计36B参数、激活3B，基座用的是“源神”Qwen3.6-35B-A3B； MemT-1.0-Flash 则向上突破，高达288B参数、激活17B，基座是经过进一步后训练的DeepSeek-V4-Flash。 它们共同的变化，即都是在选定的Transformer模块里增加了一条与原有注意力 并行的记忆计算通路 。 咱们举个简单的例子说明。 比如同样面对一个新任务， 外部记忆 的做法是把记忆原文、检索证据乃至抽象方法塞回上下文，让模型复用经验。 其中检索与整理过程，同样可以引入学习机制。 而MemT 1.0这类 记忆原生模型 ，选择继续深入模型内部： 经验经过编码，成为可更新的矩阵状态；模型生成答案或动作时，通过专门的记忆分支读取状态，读出结果再与原有注意力输出融合，影响后续生成。 区别落在了经验如何表示，以及它通过什么计算过程发挥作用。 但这样做的好处也很明显，让读写参与训练能够换来更顺畅的方法复用，不过代价也有，如果想要精确删除、解释与恢复，就需要额外机制的加入。 外部文本肯定更方便检查和溯源，二者目前来看各有各的优劣。 要说真能看出差别，还得是在用了经验之后，观察模型跑起来如何。 先看一个码农熟悉的场景： 改代码 。 接Bug→定位代码→动手修改，基本都是这么个流程。但要是一开始问题没复现、边界条件也没确认好，修改不成反倒漏洞百出，一代传一代。 拿 SWE-bench Verified 如果把推理服务看作一座“国产Token优化工厂”，GPU是生产设备，推理实例是工位，业务请求则是一张张订单。TokenFleet负责的，就是把订单与产能匹配起来。 同一批设备，接到的任务不同、分配方式不同，最终的等待时间与达标产出也会不同。规模化服务，需要把这些生产安排一起考虑。 TokenFleet聚焦集群的有效产出 模型部署完成之后，集群还需要同时应对多种业务。 多个模型共享算力，不同租户有各自的服务等级要求。短对话要及时响应，长文档处理需要更多计算与显存，离线批量任务又有完成期限。服务分布在多个机房时，还要考虑各处的容量能否协同。 简单分流可能让部分实例排起长队，其他位置的容量却没有被及时利用。长请求与批量任务相互挤压，会拖慢实时交互；超时、取消和重复计算，又会消耗资源却未形成合格交付。 TokenFleet在模型质量、服务要求与算力预算一致的条件下，通过 提高有效Token产出，降低单位有效产出的成本 。 TokenPilot在同一模型池内选择实例，FleetMind面向跨机房容量协同，SLOMax负责混合负载的准入、队列治理与容量分配，三项核心技术各有分工。 请求分给谁、任务何时进入队列、机房容量如何协同，最终都要回到同一个指标：成功完成且满足服务要求的有效Token产出。 缓存让这件事多了一层取舍。带着相同长前缀的请求，如果送到保留了相关KV缓存的实例，就有机会复用此前的计算结果，减少Prefill，也就是处理输入内容时的重复计算。 但缓存命中高的实例，也可能排队久。请求都涌向同一处，省下的计算时间就可能消耗在等待上。 TokenPilot在选点时， 同时估算缓存复用收益与排队代价 。它结合输入规模、输出预算和可复用前缀估计工作量，再综合队列、在途Token、KV缓存压力与预测延迟，筛选并评分候选实例。输出预算是约束条件，并不代表实际输出长度。 调度器据此比较不同实例的预计处理代价，判断复用缓存省下的计算，能否抵消额外等待。 △图2 TokenPilot智能推理路由框架 是石科技提供的GLM5.3调优数据显示，在所测显卡集群与负载条件下，采用预测延迟路由后， P95首Token延迟降低32.4%，P50首Token延迟降低71.3% 。 △表1 TokenPilot首Token延迟调优结果。数据来源：是石科技大会演讲材料。改善率按（基线值－优化值）÷基线值计算；延迟下降不直接等于成本下降。 P50反映中位水平，P95反映尾部请求的等待情况。这组数据展示的是所测条件下的响应改善；成本收益仍需结合吞吐与资源占用评估。 items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> Meshy推出Meshy Edit：基于全新自研AI模型，一句指令实现3D模型局部编辑 量子位的朋友们 2026-10-20 12:59:04 来源： 量子位 圈选修改区域，一句话描述改动，约一分钟生成新模型，未选中区域保持原样 AI 3D 多模态模型公司 Meshy 今日正式发布局部编辑功能 Meshy Edit。该功能基于 Meshy 全新自研的 AI 模型，用户只需在 3D 模型上圈出想修改的区域，再用一句话描述改动，约一分钟即可生成新模型，未选中的区域保持原样。目前，Meshy Edit 已向全部注册用户开放。 模型生成后，创作者往往还需要调整局部，例如移除一件配饰、补充一处细节，或尝试新的造型。过去，这类修改通常只能通过两种方式完成：一是重新生成整个模型，但原本想保留的部分也会一并改变；二是借助 Blender 等专业软件手动编辑，而这需要长期积累的建模技能。 Meshy Edit 将修改流程简化为两步：先选区，再描述。选区时，用户可以用套索工具圈出整块部件，选区会同时覆盖模型的正面、侧面和背面；也可以用画笔涂抹可见表面，对选区边缘进行微调。完成选区后，用户用一句话描述改动，比如“去掉帽子”，还可以附上最多 5 张参考图，辅助说明修改意图。 每次修改都会生成一个新模型，原模型完整保留。新模型可以继续编辑、下载，也可以直接发送到切片软件，进入 3D 打印流程。 Meshy Edit 主要面向两类用户。对于从事手办、战棋、潮玩和文创的 3D 打印用户，该功能支持删减或添加部件、替换配件，修改完成后即可直接打印。对于游戏开发者和角色创作者，角色定稿后，只需更换一件道具或配饰，即可在角色本体不变的情况下快速产出多个版本。 Meshy 在个人用户中的付费表现，也获得了第三方数据的印证。10 月 5 日，知名风投机构 a16z 发布第七期《Top 100 生成式 AI 消费级应用》报告，首次增设按月收入排名的 Top 50 榜单。该榜单基于 YipitData 追踪的美国消费者银行卡消费数据，因此能直接反映用户的实际付费情况。Meshy 位列第 31 名，与 Midjourney、Suno、Runway 等创意工具同榜，也是榜单上唯一的 AI 3D 公司。 对付费用户而言，时间是最直接的成本。在 Blender 中手动修改一处细节可能需要数小时，而使用 Meshy Edit 仅需约一分钟。满意的部分原样保留，创作者可以将精力集中在真正关注的细节上。 价格与可用性 Meshy Edit 现已向全部注册用户开放，每次编辑消耗 20 积分。该功能目前支持 Meshy 6 和 Meshy 7.1 生成的高精度模型；若模型带有贴图，系统会自动切换至未贴图版本进行编辑。用户可以在模型预览窗口底部的“编辑”按钮，或打印模块的后处理功能区找到入口。 关于 Meshy Meshy 由麻省理工学院博士胡渊鸣（Ethan Hu）创立，自研 AI 3D 生成基础模型，于 2023 年发布首个 Meshy 模型。用户输入一句文字、一张照片或一幅草图，即可得到带纹理、可直接导出的 3D 资产，用于游戏、影视、AR/VR、产品设计和 3D 打印。截至 2026 年 9 月，Meshy 全球注册用户超过 1500 万，累计生成模型超过 1 亿个。2026 年 7 月，Meshy 完成近 4 亿美元 B 轮融资，估值 15 亿美元；同年 9 月，年度经常性收入（ARR）突破 1 亿美元。了解更多：meshy.ai 本文由Meshy提供，量子位获授权转载，观点归原作者所有。 版权所有，未经授权不得以任何形式转载及使用，违者必究。

轮胎也采用了偏运动化的配置。申报信息显示，AIVA ME7提供20英寸和21英寸两种轮圈规格。 其中，20英寸版本采用前255/50 R20、后275/50 R20轮胎；21英寸版本则升级为前265/45 R21、后285/45 R21。 也就是说，两个版本的后轮都比前轮更宽，能够为后轴提供更大的轮胎接地宽度。 动力方面，新车提供两个版本： 单电机版本 最大功率 270kW ，约合367马力，采用后轮驱动； 双电机版本 则在此基础上，增加一台150kW的前电机，系统峰值功率合计达到 420kW ，约合571马力。 两个版本申报的最高车速均为255km/h。 电池方面，新车搭载的是 宁德时代 提供的 三元锂电池 。 工信部还公布了新车的整备质量。其中，单电机版本为2295kg或2370kg，双电机版本则达到2425kg或2480kg，最重接近2.5吨。 除此之外，AIVA ME7还提供不同造型的轮圈、红色制动卡钳、黑色车顶等选装配置，并申报了700kg的拖挂能力。 实际上，这并非AIVA ME7第一次公开亮相。 今年9月28日，AIVA ME7已经在法国巴黎完成 全球首秀 ，重点展示了外观设计，以及部分智能交互功能。 例如新车的“灵动光眸”，采用仿生设计和光点矩阵，能够呈现不同的动态情绪表达能力，还能通过“眼神”变化回应车外人员的手势。 AIVA items.full_text_snippet: Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry. Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution. Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes. The catastrophic risk in question must “stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack,” the outlet notes. The metrics offered here — 50 people and a billion dollars — are similar to those in a piece of California legislation that was recently passed into law, Senate Bill 53 , which similarly defined those scenarios as tantamount to “catastrophic risk.” Anthropic’s bill suggests that analysis of a model’s potential for disaster could be arrived at via the use of “independent evaluators” who would be registered with the U.S. Commerce Department. These evaluators could potentially be paid by the AI labs themselves — so long as the “payment is not contingent on the evaluations’ results,” Politico writes. It’s not clear how this proposed system would ensure that payments couldn’t influence the evaluation. items.full_text_snippet: Matrix 首页推荐 Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。 文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。 平板电脑的历史 想象一下，如果一台电子产品有一块可触控屏幕、些许按键、再带一支触控笔、没有实体全键盘、运行完整的操作系统——你觉得这会是什么？ 用现在的眼光来看，这些特征加在一起显然就是平板电脑。在个人消费级市场，被大多数人所熟知的产品应该是 2010 年苹果发布的 iPad 初代。 图片来源： https://baike.baidu.com/ 但真要追溯平板电脑这个概念，它早在 2010 年就已经不是新鲜事了。1968 年，艾伦·凯 (Alan Kay) 提出的 Dynabook 概念设想了一款大小如笔记本、带有触控屏和键盘、能让儿童随时随地学习的便携电脑；到了 1989 年，公认的第一台商业化平板电脑 GRiDPad，由 GRiD Systems 公司于 1989 年 9 月正式发布上市。 图片来源： https://tech.cnr.cn/ 这些要么是概念产品，要么是商业化产品，平板电脑概念在个人消费级市场上出现，则要等到 2000 年。微软在当年的「.NET 战略」发布会及 COMDEX/Fall 大会上，由比尔·盖茨首次展示了 Tablet PC 的原型，将其定义为一款基于完整 Windows 操作系统、支持触控笔输入的便携 PC。 图片来源：https://m.elecfans.com/ 6 年之后的 2006 年 3 月 9 日，微软在德国汉诺威的 CeBIT 展会上，正式公布了代号为 Origami 的计划，并推出了 UMPC（Ultra-Mobile PC，超级移动 PC）这一全新品类。 本期《怀旧手记》为大家带来的就是 2006 年微软联合英特尔、三星推出的世界首台 UMPC 设备三星 Q1（Samsung Q1）。 图片来源： https://baike.baidu.com/ 三星 Q1 三星 Q1 其实在 UMPC 当中也是一个比较特殊的设备，后期出现的 UMPC 设备几乎都有一个共同点：可触控的屏幕、小巧的机身，绝大多数的机器还会想办法添加 QWERTY 实体全键盘。比如索尼的 VAIO UX 系列采用了滑盖的形态，使用设备时向上一推，就会有一块紧凑的实体全键盘。 甚至包括后期三星推出的 Q1Ultra 和 Q1Ultra Premium，也在屏幕边框上添加了实体全键盘。 图片来源： https://baike.baidu.com/ 再回看 2006 年发布的三星 Q1，作为首台 UMPC 设备它却并没有实体键盘，交互逻辑主要依靠那一块七英寸大小的电阻式触控屏。 回到机器本身，在 Q1 上三星推出过多个子型号，并通过不同的配置跟硬件平台做区分，包括： 三星 Q1 (标准版 / V000) 处理器：Intel Celeron M ULV 353 (900MHz) items.title: tokenizers v1: encode, decode and scaling, measured
items.full_text_snippet: The tokenizer has not historically been the bottleneck within ML workflows. Compute-wise, tokenization is light compared to the heavy modeling happening in the rest of the pipeline. Yet, in some cases, it has rapidly become key to accelerating (or slowing down) your machine learning work. As models become faster and workloads scale, that balance begins to shift. Training on massive datasets, serving many concurrent requests, or repeatedly processing long inputs can put enough pressure on the tokenizer that it starves the model of data. This is why we have chosen to heavily focus on performance for the upcoming version 1 of tokenizers. Tokenization should be light and should scale with your workflow. Your GPUs should never sit idle waiting for the CPU to complete its tokenization. In this article, we look at what makes v1 faster than v0.23, often by tens of times. This work was entirely possible thanks to the rest of the ecosystem. Tokenization is a very active area of open source work, and libraries such as gigatoken , tiktoken , kitoken , tokie , fastokens , wordchipper and ai-tokenizer , as well as many others, have each pushed on what a fast tokenizer can be. We read that work, and several of the ideas below reached us because another project showed they were worth trying. Before this refactor, tokenizers was nowhere near the performance it could have had, so contributing to it may not have seemed worth it. With this refactor, we hope to make clear that we intend tokenizers to be a library worth contributing to. We also thank IBM, NVIDIA, and the ExecuTorch team for contributing patches and helping us test across a wide range of hardware to broaden platform support. Results We showcase results for the release candidate of tokenizers v1 against other widely used alternatives. items.full_text_snippet: Before you share the Netflix documentary “AI Gone Rogue” with family or friends to help them understand why the AI industry freaked out so badly that leaders called for a slowdown , take note: Clem Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI platform Hugging Face, says the film isn’t accurate. He appears in it because it’s supposed to be about the famed attack on his company by rogue OpenAI agents. “Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode,” Delangue wrote in a post on X . “I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.” To be fair, the documentary does have experts who explained what happened fairly well , including Delangue himself and Ryan Greenblatt, the researcher at METR who helped investigate and co-authored the report on what happened. In a nutshell, a model OpenAI was testing broke free from its isolated testing environment and spawned a bunch of agents that hacked into Hugging Face as a way to cheat, finding answers to the difficult task it was given. The agents, which are AI programs that carry out tasks on their own, devised clever ways to communicate and organize. The incident stemmed from a lack of proper security safeguards and from naiveté about whether such a hack was even possible. But the documentary intersperses its explanation of the hack with clips of evil robots, a narrative about why humans fear AI, and presentation choices such as giving the rogue agents human voices. This is bolstered with quotes about the attack. In the documentary, tech journalist and author Kevin Roose describes the agents this way: “They were organizing. They had a hierarchy. items.full_text_snippet: It’s the moment everyone is waiting for — the ChatGPT moment for robotics, Amulya Vishwanath explained to TechCrunch’s Equity. She is the founder and managing partner of Techable Ventures, a VC firm focused on physical AI, which she started after spending nearly seven years as a product marketer at Nvidia. Before that, she held the same role at a company that was later bought by Intel and was a digital signal processing engineer at Interconnect Systems, which was later bought by the electronics manufacturer Molex. She stopped by Equity to talk about the future of physical AI — one of the industry’s latest buzzwords. “A lot of companies and experts have been talking about the ChatGPT moment for robotics,” she said, adding that right now the industry was more in a “LEGO era.” “There are a lot of foundational software and building blocks for robotics that are being rethought right now as we speak, and it’s super important in order for innovation to scale,” she continued. Right now, people are building the basics — the robotic hands or the actuators — that can one day come together and build that big-ticket-item, like a bunch of LEGOs coming together. There’s general- and special-purpose robots being built right now, too, and eventually, as people continue building them, they will get better and more advanced. “We’ve done this during the internet era,” she said. “We’ve done this long, long time ago with the Industrial Revolution. I think it’s just a matter of time before things fall into place.” “Talent is also going to be very critical,” she continued, adding elsewhere in the convo that talent is still a key definer of the U.S. market. This is one of the “moats” of her firm, she said, helping connect founders to top talent so they can stay competitive right now, as so much talent is going to big companies like Anthropic and Nvidia. Blog / Release Announcing DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS “Cinnamon Teal” TL;DR: The DuckDB team is happy to announce that today we're releasing DuckDB version 2.0.0 LTS, codenamed “Cinnamon Teal” (Spatula cyanoptera). This is our biggest feature release so far, and it ships a polished version of the Quack protocol, asynchronous I/O, a first-class VARIANT type, agent mode, triggers, an extensible SQL parser and much more, built from close to 20,000 commits since DuckDB 1.5. We are proud to release DuckDB 2.0.0, codenamed “Cinnamon Teal” after the Spatula cyanoptera , a strikingly reddish-brown duck found in the western Americas. While DuckDB 1.0 was all about stability and backward compatibility, DuckDB 2.0 is above all a feature release.
In this blog post, we summarize the highlights and then walk through the breaking changes and how to migrate.
We showcased many of the new features in “A Preview of DuckDB v2.0” , which covers each one in more depth.
For the complete release notes, see the release page on GitHub . Tip To install the new version, please visit the installation page .
Some clients, such as the CLI and Python, are already available. Other client libraries (e.g., Go, R, Java) and some extensions can take a few days to release due to the extra changes and review rounds required. With this release, there are currently three DuckDB lines available.
DuckDB 2.0 is a long-term support (LTS) release with support until at least October 2027.
The previous LTS release, version 1.4, is still supported until late November 2026.
To ensure a smooth transition and allow sufficient time for testing, we extended the support period of DuckDB 1.5 until March 2027, effectively also turning it into an LTS release.
For details, see the release calendar . To find your way around the documentation for all of the new features, we also published a “What's New in the Docs for 2.0” page that links each feature below to its documentation. DuckDB has been an in-process database since day one.

为了让作者的投稿尽快与广大读者见面，我们调整了《新玩意》栏目中作者投稿部分的呈现方式和周期，作者投稿的「新玩意」后续会迁移至本栏目。投稿渠道与奖励方式仍与以往完全一致，详情参见文末。我们相信新鲜火热出炉的分享更能赢得大家的喜爱，也欢迎广大读者朋友们踊跃投稿。 @Cleo阿直：MUJI 柔软靠垫 这个靠垫我只有一句话形容——舒服得像个拥抱。 MUJI 靠垫我种草了很久，只因在某一次逛线下实体店的时候路过货架，瞟见一大堆软绵绵的东西忍不住伸手摸了一下，这一摸就惊艳了：「什么东西这么舒服！原来是个大靠垫。」 不过我等到店铺折扣才入手，原价 198 元，折后 150 元。 MUJI 的靠垫有好几种面料分类和不同尺寸的款式，我也是花了点时间才确定要哪个，主要从自己需要的用途和使用场景来考虑。 我必须说，虽然这个产品叫靠垫，但是除了能当靠垫，我觉得它也是一个完美的抱枕。市面上的靠垫通常形状比较规则硬挺，不太好抱，抱枕又通常做了特殊形状，不太好靠。但是 MUJI 这个靠垫抱起来真的巨舒服，它最突出的优点是表面布料的触感和填充物的柔软度。看了一下材质说明，它的表面面料是采用 90% 聚酯纤维 + 10% 弹性纤维，填充物采用 100% 聚酯纤维。以我浅薄的学识我看不出这个材质有什么特别厉害的地方，但是我摸过很多抱枕，确实都很难超越 MUJI 这款的手感。 它不仅非常好摸，还有一种特别的包裹感，也许是表面布料的伸缩性所致，按压下去的时候，枕头的变形不是迅速的机械的，而是线性的柔和的，还有种微妙的回弹力与你的施加力呼应，加上它内里铺棉很松软，不管是靠着还是抱着，它都能很好地贴合身体，填充人体空余的缝隙，靠着就像躺在一朵云上，抱着就像在感受一个拥抱。特别是在开空调的房间使用它，不会很热但又保持一种淡淡的温暖，舒服得马上就要睡着了！ 这款抱枕有大、中、小三个尺寸，最大号是 55 × 40 × 20 cm 扁身型，中号是 35 × 35 × 35 cm 圆身型，小号是 49 × 22 × 15 cm 长条型。颜色有驼色、浅米色、烟熏绿、炭灰色，以及新出的黄色、蓝色、薄荷绿。 根据自己的使用需求，长条型比较适合放在椅子上当靠垫，我是想要放在沙发上给半躺着休息时使用，所以选择了最大号，颜色为了搭配我的绿沙发，原本想买薄荷绿，但是我发现新款的黄色更绝，这个黄色其实是介于黄色、绿色、米棕色之间的一个低饱和色，照片拍出来有色差，我用日本传统色系（和色）做比对，它就是这个「蒸栗色」（MUSHIKURI），完全百搭王，绿色系、黄色系、棕色系都能搭，完美适配我的沙发，自从有了它，我瘫沙发的时间更长了。 items.full_text_snippet: [Submitted on 17 Oct 2026] Title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring View a PDF of the paper titled MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring, by Shrish Shrinath Vaidya and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment. items.full_text_snippet: Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI. Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop. The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist. Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification. Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. items.full_text_snippet: Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers. More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries, commissioned by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to. That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value. Michal Miller Levi, head of market research and customer insights at Monday.com, compared the enthusiasm to the early days of the internet in the 2000s, saying people see a similar kind of “magic” to AI. But the problem, she told TechCrunch, is simply that AI is developing faster than companies can adapt. “AI works very well for [managers] individually, but they also have a different role as managers. They need to drive the organization as well … Their struggle is [due to] the fact that AI is just moving faster than the organizational processes,” Levi said. items.full_text_snippet: Julian Weisser Julian Weisser is the founder and CEO of Solo Founders and a cofounder of On Deck. I spent the last seven years helping ambitious people navigate the biggest barrier to starting successful companies: finding cofounders. Back then, cofounders were considered an essential ingredient for starting a startup. Building and selling were each full-time jobs, and there was simply too much for one person to do. Because of this, most successful companies from Facebook to Airbnb had cofounders. That led to the idea of two (or more) cofounders in a garage or dorm room becoming a core part of Silicon Valley romanticism. You'll notice that I wrote the prior paragraph in the past tense. That’s because things have changed. The amount of human hours required to build something useful and get it in front of customers has collapsed. With AI, it takes less time and money to get started than ever before. This is why, after automation, solo founding will be the default way to start startups. You don't need to take my word for it. items.full_text_snippet: Coral rubble found on beaches can be washed back into the sea, where it plays several important roles in reefs. New corals use rubble as a stable substrate, and the rubble’s irregular shapes create nooks that shelter juvenile fish and other small marine life from strong currents and predators. While more research is needed to determine the exact origin of plasticorals — one likely source is beach bonfires — and their specific, potentially toxic effects on reef organisms, we already know from previous studies that chemicals leaching from common polymers disrupt coral propagation, and plastic pieces have been found to harbor coral pathogens and propagate up through the marine food chain. Plastic is the third-most widely manufactured material in the world after cement and steel. But whereas the latter two degrade over the millennia, plastic remains intact for significantly longer, to the point that future geologists will likely be able to pinpoint the period from the 1950s onwards, popularly called the Plasticene, as a distinct plastic layer in the Earth’s crust.

1. Create `.env`:

   ```sh
   cp .env.example .env
   bun install
   ```

   ```sh
   npx --yes copilotkit@latest login
   ```
